title: Breast MRI
what: Images of the breasts in a magnetic field, with contrast dye into a vein. No radiation.
why: To clarify findings after a mammogram and ultrasound, for a high family risk, with breast implants, or before surgery.
duration: usually 20 to 40 minutes; the report in 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: A pacemaker, defibrillator, or other implant with electronics
Metal in your body: joint replacements, plates, clips on blood vessels, or shrapnel
If you are or might be pregnant
If you are afraid of closed spaces. Your doctor will suggest ways to help

prepare.title: Cycle day
prepare.text: Best on day 7 to 14 of your cycle. After menopause, any day. Ask your doctor.

prepare.title: Contrast
prepare.text: If contrast is ordered, a creatinine test is sometimes needed. Usually no food for 2 to 4 hours. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Metal
prepare.text: Take off everything metal: jewelry, watches, hair clips, piercings. Leave your phone and cards in the locker.

bring: Past mammograms, breast ultrasounds, and MRIs
steps: You undress to the waist and leave metal in the locker
An IV line is put in a vein in your arm
You lie on your stomach with your breasts in a special coil with openings
Your head rests on a support, with your arms forward or at your sides
The machine knocks loudly. You get headphones or earplugs
Lie still. Staff talk to you over an intercom
Halfway through, contrast is given and more images are taken
feel: It does not hurt, but it is loud and tight
Lying on your stomach can be uncomfortable. Say so, and pillows will be added
With contrast: a cool feeling in the vein
after: You can go back to your day right away
After contrast, drink more water, unless your doctor said otherwise
Take the report to a breast specialist
red_flags: After contrast: itching, a rash, a swollen face, or trouble breathing. Tell the staff right away or call emergency services

faq.q: Why does the cycle day matter?
faq.a: In the second half of the cycle, breast tissue changes and takes up more contrast. The images are less accurate.
Usually yes. If unsure, ask your doctor.

reminders.text: Breast MRI tomorrow. Bring past mammograms and ultrasounds, and take off jewelry.
